mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS decreases by > 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO increases over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure that erodes consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combined effect signals a restrictive monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, the combined signal indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month and PAYEMS increases > 200,000
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decrease by more than 10% month-over-month and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) decrease by more than 1% month-over-month, the combined signal indicates weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 10% month-over-month and RSAFS decreases > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances when both conditions are met.
